instructions: Peel the potatoes and coarsely grate them into a large bowl. Don't rinse them. The starch holds the crique together.
Mince the garlic and chop 1/2 cup of the parsley. Add the garlic, 6 tbsp of the parsley, the egg, 1 tsp salt and the pepper to the potatoes. Mix with your hands until it's evenly combined.
Heat two 10-inch nonstick skillets over medium. Add 3 tbsp oil to each pan.
Divide the potato mixture between the pans and press it into an even layer about 1/2 inch thick. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and the edges look crisp.
Slide each crique onto a plate. Add 1 tbsp oil to each pan, then slide the crique back in, uncooked side down. Cook for 10 minutes, until golden.
Meanwhile, whisk 2 tbsp oil, the juice of half the lemon and 1/4 tsp salt in a large bowl. Toss in the salad greens.
Taste a corner of the crique. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Transfer each to a board, sprinkle with the remaining 2 tbsp parsley and cut into wedges.
method_notes: Grated potato, garlic and parsley fried slowly until golden and crisp is what every version shares. The lead (Obviously French) fries in olive oil and butter; here it's all olive oil to keep it dairy-free, and the egg it lists as optional is in for a firmer crique. The garlic is 2 cloves rather than the lead's 1, and the 10 to 15 minute rest is skipped to stay inside the time. No rated page was readable, so this is a fallback lead.
